subject: SLA template: request to relax uptime floor & credit cap for high-throughput jobs
messages:
From: Allison Park <contracts@nexahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nexahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA template - request on uptime bands and monthly credits

Marissa,

Thanks for sending the updated SLA template. Our legal and SRE teams reviewed and we have two specific asks before we can sign:

1) For bulk batch inference jobs (nightly model refresh and bulk embedding pipelines) that run at high concurrency and high token rates, we want to carve out the uptime floor from 99.95% to 99.9% — these jobs are latency-tolerant and we prefer a cost/availability tradeoff.

2) We need a hard cap on monthly service credits at 15% of monthly subscription spend. Your current template has an open-ended credit formula that could materially exceed our budget for peak months.

Can Redwood accept these two adjustments as a contract-level exception? If not, can you propose alternate mitigations (credits cap + prioritized maintenance windows + assigned escalation SLA)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window closes next Friday.

Best,
Allison Park
Sr. Contracts Manager | Nexa Health
contracts@nexahealth.com

Attachments: Example_SRE_Traffic_Profile.csv (referenced)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Allison Park <contracts@nexahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template - request on uptime bands and monthly credits

Allison —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level response below; I copied Ben (sales ops) and Laura (legal) so we can formalize.

1) Batch workload carveout: We can agree to a documented carveout for specific workload classes ("BatchHeavy") where the uptime floor is 99.9% instead of 99.95%, provided that:
  - Nexa identifies the job IDs and routes them to a designated pool (reserved or burst)
  - Redwood receives a technical annex describing traffic profile (peak qps, typical seq length)

2) Credit cap: Redwood is comfortable with a capped credit at 15% of monthly subscription for these BatchHeavy exceptions, but we need to preserve standard credit math for the rest of the services. In exchange we request a 60-day notice for any workload reclassification and an agreed list of maintenance windows that will not trigger credits.

Next steps: Ben / Laura — can we confirm contract language (SLA section + Annex B for workload list)? If accepted, I will prepare the redline and a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example.com

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood SLA template - request on uptime bands and monthly credits

Marissa / Laura —

Looping in procurement ops commentary: I ran rough $ impact numbers against the HP-9842-NEXA commitment. If we accept 15% credit cap for BatchHeavy and allow 99.9% floor for that class only, our expected worst-case credit exposure increases by ~0.6% of ARR for the first 12 months given Nexa's projected burst patterns. That's acceptable within our margin model if we require the reserved-routing + annex.

Laura — for the legal redline: draft language to include these elements: definition of "BatchHeavy" (by job id or tag), credit cap clause (15% monthly cap only for BatchHeavy), maintenance window carveouts, and a 60-day reclassification notice. Also include an index of the Annex with a link to the workload list.

If legal is good, I'll approve the commercial concession.

—Ben
Director, Sales Operations
ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Attachment suggested: Maintenance_Window_Annex.docx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template - request on uptime bands and monthly credits

Ben / Marissa —

Draft redline below (high level summary pasted into this thread):

- Define "BatchHeavy" workloads: Job or queue identifiers maintained in Annex B; workloads routed to a designated pool are eligible for the lower uptime floor.
- Uptime floor for BatchHeavy: 99.9% monthly measurement window. For all other services, default 99.95%.
- Credits for BatchHeavy: limited to 15% of monthly subscription fees attributable to the BatchHeavy services for the month in which the breach occurs. The aggregate monthly credit for the Account across all services shall not exceed 15% unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Maintenance carveouts: routine maintenance windows listed in Annex B shall not be eligible for credit; Redwood will provide 14 days' notice for any planned maintenance that impacts BatchHeavy pools.
- Reclassification: Customer must provide 60 calendar days' notice plus traffic evidence for any reclassification requests; Redwood reserves the right to validate with telemetry.
- Audit & dispute: Credits calculated per standard formula; disputes escalated to named contacts with a 30-day resolution window.

I'll attach a tracked-change redline in the repo and will prep the DocuSign-ready exhibit once we have explicit acceptance from Nexa.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.example.com

Attachment: SLA_redline_annotated.docx (will upload to link)

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: SLA exception for BatchHeavy workloads and 15% monthly credit cap

Allison / Tom —

Thanks for the quick review and for sharing the traffic profile. Per our internal review (Ben / Laura / Aditya copied), Redwood can accept the following contract-level exception:

Summary of agreed exception (to be captured in Annex B):
- "BatchHeavy" workloads (explicit job IDs provided by Nexa) will be subject to a monthly uptime floor of 99.9% measured against BatchHeavy-tagged requests.
- Monthly service credit for BatchHeavy incidents will be capped at 15% of the monthly fees attributed to BatchHeavy services. Aggregate account credits across all services will not exceed 15% of monthly subscription spend unless otherwise agreed.
- Routine maintenance windows that affect the BatchHeavy pool are listed in Annex B and are excluded from credit calculations; Redwood will provide 14 days' notice for such maintenance.
- Customer must provide 60 days' notice and traffic evidence for workload reclassification; Redwood will validate via telemetry prior to granting changes.

Next steps: Laura will upload the tracked redline and I will send a DocuSign envelope containing the SLA exhibit + Annex B today. Can you confirm we have Nexa's definitive job ID list for Annex B by EOD Thursday (13 May)? If so, we'll finalize and route to signature.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the Annex together.

Best,
Marissa Cole
